producer_report.summary:
I added two prose-only defaults, `version-pins` and `hermetic-checks`, to defaults.toml. I raised the reader budget from 2,000 to 2,200 tokens and recorded the decision as D181.

The root cause is that defaults.toml said nothing on version-pin or ambient-tool policy, so the reader asked the user about both. The reader sees only each entry's first sentence, so the stance sits there. The `version-pins` sentence names `cargo run -p xtask -- repin` for the Claude Code pin (`claude_version`) only, because that is the one line the command rewrites. No command was built.

With both entries the reader set measures 2156 of 2200, taken from the budgets test. `docs/system-facts.md` now says that, and `BudgetSet::Reader` returns 2_200. The reader row in `run_pin_tests.rs` now reads the budget constant instead of the literal 2000.

D181 and the CHANGELOG entry state the departure from D170's rule, with D93 as precedent. They also record that `pages.yml` still uses floating action tags, with a follow-up job proposed. I left workflows alone.

The new test `pin_and_hermetic_check_defaults_reach_the_reader` parses the real defaults.toml and checks both ids, their key phrases and the exact rendered lines.

The targeted test sets I ran all pass, clippy is clean, and the full `cargo test --locked` run finished with exit code 0. I could not read that run's output, so the exit code is my only evidence for it.

checks_run.note: First run flagged one assert in the new test; cargo fmt --all fixed it. Clippy ran after the fix.

checks_run.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets --test backtest --test mirrors

checks_run.note: Ran past the 1200 s foreground limit and was moved to the background. The completion notice reported exit code 0. I could not read its output file, so the exit code is my only evidence for this run.

checks_run.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets system_facts_budgets_match_computed (before the facts edit)
checks_run.note: Failed as expected, reading 'computed value is 2156 of 2200'. I copied that figure into docs/system-facts.md.

criteria_check.criterion: defaults.toml has a new [[default]] entry id version-pins whose first sentence says pins are exact, never auto-floated, and changed only by the person running Athena through the existing `cargo run -p xtask -- repin` command; scoped to code, config and build and marked prose-only.
criteria_check.evidence: git diff -- defaults.toml shows the entry. Its first sentence reads 'Version pins are exact and never auto-floated; only the person running Athena moves one, and the Claude Code pin (`claude_version`) moves through the existing `cargo run -p xtask -- repin` command.' applies_to is [code, config, build], and the statement ends 'Prose-only: no loop code enforces it yet.' The new test pin_and_hermetic_check_defaults_reach_the_reader asserts the exact rendered line and passed (cargo test -p athena-data). The sentence ties repin to `claude_version` because that is the only line the command rewrites; the Rust channel and the other pins have no command, which the second sentence says.

criteria_check.criterion: defaults.toml has a new [[default]] entry id hermetic-checks whose first sentence says a check never depends on inherited environment or ambient tools, the runner passes every path a check needs, and any preferred-versus-fallback tool choice is recorded in the check output; marked prose-only. defaults.toml is the only governance file changed (athena.toml, workflows, xtask unchanged per git diff).
criteria_check.evidence: git diff -- defaults.toml shows the hermetic-checks entry with applies_to [code, config, build, tests]. Its first sentence matches the criterion text and it carries the 'Prose-only' marker. git diff --stat lists exactly seven files: CHANGELOG.md, crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs, crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs, crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs, defaults.toml, docs/decisions.md and docs/system-facts.md. athena.toml, workflows and xtask are not among them.

criteria_check.criterion: The reader budget at crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs is raised to about 2200, and the literal at crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs (~1625) and any figure in docs/system-facts.md match it.
criteria_check.evidence: lib.rs returns BudgetSet::Reader => 2_200, with the comment reworded to name the reader-only rise (D93, D181). run_pin_tests.rs now formats '{} of {} tokens used' with BudgetSet::Reader.budget() in place of the literal 2000. docs/system-facts.md reads 'budget reader: 2156 of 2200', the size the budgets test computed. cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets (7 passed) and cargo test -p athena-core --lib run_pin_tests (52 passed) both pass.

criteria_check.criterion: docs/decisions.md gets a new appended decision D181 with a Provenance bullet naming the root cause, jobs 20261016-005805-p806 and 20261025-183644-t67q, and stating it departs from D170's rule that budgets never rise to fit a set; no existing entry is edited. CHANGELOG.md has an entry naming the root cause (defaults silent on pin and ambient-tool policy). No repin command is built.
criteria_check.evidence: git diff -- docs/decisions.md shows 34 added lines and no deletions, appended after D180. The D181 Provenance bullet names the root cause, both jobs and the retry 20261114-012353-pbvc, and states the departure from D170. It also records the pages.yml floating-tag gap and a follow-up proposal. The CHANGELOG diff is one entry added at the top of Unreleased/Added, naming the same root cause. No xtask file changed. cargo test -p athena-cli --test backtest (21), -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus and --test buy_first (24 and 12), and -p athena-cli --test mirrors (4) pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a new test in crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs parses the real defaults.toml, asserts both ids exist with key phrases (exact, never auto-floated, repin, ambient), and asserts the rendered reader prompt contains both; it fails on the base tree and passes with the change. The reader prompt budget tests, budgets tests and xtask policy test also pass.
criteria_check.evidence: pin_and_hermetic_check_defaults_reach_the_reader parses REPO_DEFAULTS (the real defaults.toml) and asserts both ids, their applies_to, the key phrases and the two exact rendered lines. It passed in cargo test --locked -p athena-data. On the base tree get("version-pins").unwrap() panics, so the test fails there; I reasoned this from the base file and did not run it against the base. The budgets (7), run_pin_tests (52) and xtask policy (22) targets pass. The whole-suite `cargo test --locked` run completed with exit code 0 (reported by the background-task notice; output not readable).

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` (warnings denied); both pass. Recorded checks on the final tree also count.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I also ran cargo fmt --all --check (clean after cargo fmt --all) and cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings (finished with no warnings).

open_issues: The three actions in .github/workflows/pages.yml still use floating major tags. This is recorded in D181 and the CHANGELOG, with a follow-up job proposed. Workflows are not deliverables here, so nothing changed.
mistakes: My first full-suite command used a malformed redirect and was denied. I did not retry that command; I ran targeted test sets instead, then a plain `cargo test --locked`.
The full `cargo test --locked` run passed the 1200 s foreground limit and I could not read its background output; only its exit code 0 (from the completion notice) is my evidence.
learnings: DefaultsModel::render prints only the first sentence of each entry, cut at the first '. ', so the stance must sit in sentence one.
The budgets test failure message gives the computed reader size: 2156 of 2200 with the two new entries.
The producer's shell blocks tail, grep, here-documents and a redirect placed before other arguments; use the Read, Grep and Edit tools instead.
Appending to docs/decisions.md works through Edit anchored on the last D180 lines.
desires: A way to read a background task's output file, or a longer foreground limit for the full suite.
